newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Amnesty says executions soared in 1996, China led.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty says executions soared in 1996, China led.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Friday that the number of executions in the world hit a record high of more than 4,200 in 1996 and urged countries to join a U.N. human rights motion on scrapping capital punishment.
China led the way with more than 3,500 executions in 1996, followed by Ukraine, Russia and Iran, it said in a statement.

The human rights group said the number of prisoners executed in 1996 jumped 30 percent over 1995 and the number of people sentenced to death also rose sharply to 7,017 from 4,165 -- the highest annual figures Amnesty said it had ever recorded.

Amnesty noted that China was making increased use of the death penalty since it launched a "strike hard" anti-crime drive last April. Most prisoners did not receive fair trials and many were executed soon after their sentence was pronounced, it said.
"Despite a growing acceptance that the death penalty has no place in a modern society, a hard core of countries continue to execute people in increasing numbers," Amnesty said.
It said a U.N. resolution urging nations to abolish capital punishment, passed in Geneva on Thursday, was a reminder to such countries that "the weight of world opinion is against them".

The United States was the only Western nation to vote against the motion, sponsored by Italy and passed with a simple majority of 27 in favour, 11 against and 14 abstentions at the U.N. Human Rights Commission. It is not legally binding.
Last year, the respected International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) accused the United States of carrying out death sentences that were arbitrary and racially discriminatory against blacks.
It said blacks made up 40 percent of U.S. executions in 1973-1995 and 44 percent of the U.S. jail population. Americans of African origin made up six percent of the U.S. population.
Amnesty said 3,150 prisoners were on death row in the United States last September, and 45 prisoners were executed in 1996.
China voted against the U.N. motion, as did Algeria, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Egypt, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Pakistan and South Korea.
Britain was the only European Union member state to abstain, along with countries like Zaire, Cuba, Pakistan and India.
Amnesty said Ukraine executed 169 prisoners in 1996, Russia executed at least 140 and Iran some 110. Unconfirmed reports said Turkmenistan had 123 executions Iraq many others, it said.

Amnesty said 58 countries had abolished capital punishment for all crimes. Belgium was the latest to do so in 1996. Another 15 countries had scrapped capital punishment for common crimes and 27 had suspended executions for 10 years or more.
